falsePositive.title: Dark roof + wet pavement read as structural damage
falsePositive.analystReason: Roof edge is intact; the dark shape is water reflection.
falsePositive.correction: Water reflection — not a collapsed roof. Finding rejected.
falsePositive.lesson: The model was confident. The analyst was right. This is why a human signs the assessment.
falsePositive.narrative: The top-ranked site is a false positive: a dark roof and wet pavement read as structural damage. The analyst rejects it with a visible reason, the ranking re-orders, and a team is freed.

audience.prompt: Team 3 is free. Where does it go?

a.name: Heppingen Substation
a.consequence: Power stays on for 8,400,000 EUR of asset value; the dense housing block stays uncovered.

b.name: Bachem Valley Road
b.consequence: 1,250 people and 3,600,000 EUR of value get a team; the power asset stays on the watch list.

audience.tradeoff: A substation on open road keeps power on. Dense housing keeps people safe. Both are defensible; the room decides.

assessment.title: GeoResponse assessment — Ahr valley flood
assessment.summary: Ahr valley flood affects 40 km². 18 priority sites remain after review; 0 finding(s) were rejected by an analyst. The top three sites (S01, S02, S03) carry €61,000,000 of exposed value and 11,730 people within 700 m. Three response teams are allocated by urgency, access and value at risk.
assessment.headline: The highest-ranked site is Ahrweiler Altstadt (S01), severity red, confidence 94%. A 11,800 m² change intersects blocked access; 2,100 people live within 700 m and the insured value is €4,800,000.
limitations: Change extent is derived from a simulated Sentinel-2-like 10 m composite in the demo pack; production uses licensed imagery.
Dark roofs, wet pavement and deep shadow can mimic structural damage; every rejection is retained in the audit trail.
Population is a 700 m radius estimate from the demo population grid, not a household count.
No site is approved automatically. A human analyst signs the assessment before any claim or dispatch decision.
